quote: As by learning the alphabets one can, through practice, master all the sciences, so by thoroughly practising first the (physical) training, one acquires the Knowledge of the True.
meaning: Learn the ABC, keep practising, and one day you can read anything. Practice first, and understanding follows.

quote: The truth is, I had to work very hard... to make it look easy. I spent years whining... swearing... throwing my racket... before I learned to keep my cool.
meaning: Federer won only 54% of the points in his 1,526 singles matches. Years of work and mistakes made it look easy.

quote: ...without consuming the juice of the divine nectar, how can we know the taste of the fruit? This is never possible.
meaning: You only know a fruit's taste by eating it. Yoga is the same: you learn it by doing it.

quote: I was never able to make a fact my own without seeing it... All the work had to be my own.
meaning: In 1805 Faraday became a bookbinder's apprentice. He did simple chemistry experiments that cost a few pence a week.

quote: ...intellectual power and a knowledge of the scriptures alone do not lead to Self-realization... Practice alone is the path to atma labhah [gaining the Self].
meaning: Reading and smart thinking are not enough. Practice is the path. Jois began yoga at 12, in 1927.

quote: ...no sudden inspiration can replace the long toil which is indispensable... to render the hand obedient to the commands of feeling.
meaning: Paris's top art school said no to Rodin three times. He learned by working as a craftsman for about twenty years.

who: Wang Yangming · Instructions for Practical Life
quote: The situation may be likened to a man traveling. When (by walking) he has covered a stage, he understands that stage... In this way he gradually reaches his destination.
meaning: A traveller understands each part of the road only by walking it, and step by step he arrives.

quote: Wisdom is the daughter of experience.
meaning: Leonardo started as a studio boy at about 14. By 1472, at age 20, he was a master painter.

quote: I cannot describe the grandeur of this contemplation. He who practises, knows.
meaning: Some things words cannot explain. Do the practice, and you will understand it yourself.

quote: With every repetition you will discover some hitherto unnoticed defect... Obviate these defects, one by one, and in so doing you will come nearer and nearer to the spiritual essence...
meaning: In 21 concerts, Hofmann played 255 different works from memory. He taught that each repeat shows one more thing to fix.
